Attacker-supplied cookie/form values are echoed back as raw HTML/JavaScript and also persisted in the cookie via response.set_cookie, causing XSS.

extra.message: The 'next' query parameter is taken directly from request.args and passed to redirect() without validation. An attacker can supply an external URL (e.g., ?next=https://evil.com) to redirect users to a malicious site (open redirect, useful for phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: MessagesView.post() lacks the @admin_required decorator used on the other methods in the same class. Any unauthenticated remote user can create arbitrary Message records with attacker-controlled 'message' and 'from_user' fields, which are later rendered unescaped in the admin panel (stored XSS) and pollute admin data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source ('Keep it secret, keep it safe'). Anyone with access to the code can forge signed session cookies (e.g., impersonate any user or set session values such as admin state), defeating session integrity.

Flask DEBUG mode is enabled in application configuration (app.config['DEBUG'] = True). In production this exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger and detailed stack traces, which can allow remote code execution and sensitive information disclosure.

User passwords are stored as a plain string column with no hashing. Login (app/blueprints/login/views.py:17) and change_password (app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:34-36) compare/store passwords in cleartext. A database compromise exposes all user passwords directly.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: User.serialize includes the plaintext 'password' field and is returned by the UsersView API endpoints (app/blueprints/api/views.py:72). This exposes user passwords over the API (sensitive data exposure).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The add_admin management command defaults the admin password to 'admin' (username 'admin' with password 'admin'). If invoked without arguments, the application is deployed with well-known default credentials, allowing trivial admin account takeover (is_admin is granted solely for username == 'admin', app/models/models.py:21).

The after_request handler sets the 'X-XSS-Protection: 0' response header for all requests whenever the session flag is not enabled (the default), explicitly disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter and increasing the impact of the XSS vulnerabilities in this application.

State-changing POST endpoints (change_password, change_email, send_feedback, login, and API POST handlers) implement no CSRF token validation and the app does not use Flask-WTF/CSRFProtect. Forms in account_area.html contain no CSRF tokens, so an attacker can perform cross-site request forgery to change a victim's password/email while they are logged in.
